newsitem.title: CANADA: Royal Bank Canada announces share buyback.
newsitem.headline: Royal Bank Canada announces share buyback.

text.p: Royal Bank of Canada said on Thursday that it intends to buyback up to 10 percent of the public float of its common shares.
Canada's largest bank said in a statement that it has a public float of about 313 million common shares.

The share repurchase program is intended to offset any dilution arising from the proposed acquisition of Toronto-based brokerage firm Richardson Greenshields of Canada Ltd for C$480 million, the bank said.
Royal Bank's stock was trading up 0.95 at 36.10 in midday turnover of 435,000 shares on the Toronto Stock Exchange.
Based on the current value of the bank's stock, the total share buyback is worth about C$1.1 billion.

"Our goal is to maximize shareholder returns over the long term and we believe the repurchase of our shares is consistent with that objective," said Royal Bank chairman and chief executive officer John Cleghorn. Under the terms of the deal announced in August, Richardson Greenshields' shareholders can take up C$240 million in cash, with the balance payable in shares exchangeable for Royal Bank common shares.
The Richardson Greenshields acquisition is expected to close on November 1.
The bank said it will make the share repurchases from time to time in the open market at market prices.
Royal Bank is the latest major Canadian bank to announce a huge share buyback.
In July, Toronto-Dominion Bank said it plans to repurchase up to 10 percent of its common shares.
